headers.orientation: With USB-C at the bottom: front/component face, P1 is the right header; pin 1 is at the top outer/right corner, odd pins run down the outer/right column and even pins down the inner/left column. Rear/silkscreen face, P1 is the left header; pin 1 is at the top outer/left corner, odd pins run down the outer/left column and even pins down the inner/right column.

With USB-C at the bottom: front/component face, P2 is the left header; pin 1 is at the top inner/right corner, odd pins run down the inner/right column and even pins down the outer/left column. Rear/silkscreen face, P2 is the right header; pin 1 is at the top inner/left corner, odd pins run down the inner/left column and even pins down the outer/right column.

With USB-C at the bottom: front/component face, P3 is the top-right SWD header; left to right it is pin 4 GND, pin 3 SWCLK, pin 2 SWDIO, pin 1 3.3V. Rear/silkscreen face, P3 is at the top left; left to right it is pin 1 3.3V, pin 2 SWDIO, pin 3 SWCLK, pin 4 GND.

reading_guide.title: Use the same landmark from either face
reading_guide.text: Keep the USB-C connector end at the bottom in both views. The front/component face is shown on board drawing pages 1 and 2; the rear/silkscreen face is page 3. Flip about the vertical axis to compare them: left and right exchange places, while the inner/outer columns stay inner/outer. P1 and P2 each count top to bottom in 22 rows, pins 1/2 through 43/44.

reading_guide.title: Find hidden pad identifiers in the PDF text layer
reading_guide.text: Open the original board PDF in a text-search-capable PDF viewer and go to page 1. Use Find for the full Altium pad identifier: PAP101 is P1 pin 1, PAP1030 is P1 pin 30, PAP201 is P2 pin 1 and PAP301 is P3 pin 1. These identifiers are hidden PDF text, not visibly printed pad numbers; a search highlight locates the pad. Select the exact token (or use whole-word search), because PAP101 can also match the prefix of PAP1010. The identifiers follow PA + header ID + 0 + pin number. Do not identify pin 1 from pad shape alone: P2 pin 44 (PAP2044) and P3 pin 4 (PAP304) are also square, in addition to each header's pin 1.

sources.block: Hidden Altium pad identifiers PAP101-PAP1044, PAP201-PAP2044 and PAP301-PAP304

reading_guide.title: Read the offset rear legends using their matching white dots
reading_guide.text: Three rear header rows have their legends printed farther inboard. A white dot beside each row matches a white dot at the end of a short line above its offset legend. With USB-C at the bottom, read each pair left to right from the rear: upper-left P1 pins 1/2 are G 5V (GND / 5V); upper-right P2 pins 1/2 are G 3V3 (GND / 3V3); lower-left P1 pins 43/44 are B13 B12 (PB13 / PB12). Keep all six as silkscreen labels for those existing contacts, not additional headers. The rear drawing establishes the markings and dot convention; the schematic independently establishes the nets. These six legend/contact nets were not individually continuity-tested in the guided review.

onboard_connections.description: MCU NRST; reset button SW3 and C4. U9 MAX809 reset via R4; SYS_RESET through R1 (330 ohm) feeds camera DVP_RST (J2 pin 6) and TFT LCD_RESET (J3 pin 3). Both reboot and dfu call NVIC_SystemReset (SYSRESETREQ/SFTRESET). RM0433 §8.4.2, Figure 43 describes an internal reset pulse generator with a minimum 20 µs pulse propagated to NRST. A button press and software reboot were captured at external P2:10 (NR); the reboot trace spent approximately 26 µs near zero at that contact. This observation is separate from the specified internal pulse duration. dfu and the downstream TFT/camera reset lines remain unmeasured. This reset-controller effect is not a GPIO assignment.
onboard_connections.condition: External NR button/reboot behavior observed; R1/SYS_RESET continuation and downstream reset behavior remain drawing evidence, with fitted component values unverified

sources.block: DCMI / SYS_RESET to DVP_RST / J2 pin 6
TFT LCD / SYS_RESET to LCD_RESET / J3 pin 3

bench_observations.result: At the external P2:10 (NR) contact, rest voltage was approximately 3.3 V; a physical reset-button press held NR low for 157.5 ms. Software reboot spent approximately 26 µs near zero. Falling edge to 1.65 V on recovery was approximately 114 µs; start of rise to 3.0 V was approximately 524 µs, with return to approximately 3.3 V around 1 ms.
bench_observations.limits: These intervals use different cursor endpoints at NR and do not measure internal MCU reset duration. dfu, downstream TFT/camera reset lines, peripheral response and the cause of the recovery shape remain unmeasured. Acquisition and cursors were saved on the Rigol; raw export is unconfirmed.

notes: All 92 exposed pin-header contacts P1/P2/P3 are included once. FPC/USB/microSD mating contacts are identified as onboard connectors rather than additional pin headers.

Owner-reported module revisions and bench setup are recorded in audit.json. Per-contact and per-connection observations below identify the measured Board A C8/SB3 segments, inconclusive D13 probe, external NR traces and representative normal heartbeat evidence. Other paths remain drawing/source evidence; fitted component identification/values remain unverified.

The board drawing contains front and mirrored rear views. Use page 1 PDF text search for hidden pad identifiers and the USB-C-bottom orientations above; page 1 does not visibly print pad numbers, and square pads are not unique pin-1 marks.
Do not infer a malfunction from a shared net. Firmware-PC8/microSD D0 and diagnostic-PD13/QSPI IO3 are actual overlaps, with assembly/functional consequences untested.
Vendor net names USB1_DN/USB1_DP are schematic names: on STM32H743 PA11/PA12 serve USB2_OTG_FS, not the PB14/PB15 USB1 controller. Do not infer controller identity from the vendor net prefix.
U7 and U8 are drawn as separate W25Qxx devices, each default W25Q64 64 Mbit / 8 MB. Actual flash device identification and capacity remain unverified.
